images.caption: Wakefield Cathedral A church has stood on the site of Wakefield Cathedral in Kirkgate since Saxon times. The present building was built in the 14th century and restored in the 19th century, and is a grade I listed building. The parish church of All Saints was elevated to cathedral status when Wakefield became a city in 1888.

images.caption: Sundial. This sundial can be found on the south side of Wakefield Cathedral, West Yorkshire, England. I can only assume it was fashioned from stonework recovered from an earlier version of the then parish church, as I can find no documentation on it. Note the boot scraper, another relic from the past.

images.caption: Railings, Wakefield Cathedral The C19 grade II listed structure on the northern boundary of the Cathedral grounds consists of a low stone plinth supporting cast iron railings with curved cruciform standards, cast iron stays and urn finials at intervals.

images.caption:
11 ft pinnacle from All Saints church, now Wakefield cathedral, removed during repairs in the 1860s, and is currently exhibited in the Art Gallery grounds. Ref. 1191552
Sir George Gilbert Scott, worked on the cathedral between 1857 and 1874. His involvement included re-casing the tower in 1859 and rebuilding the spire in 1860. This was followed by major external repairs, and finally the nave was completed in 1874. Ref 1075648

images.caption: German Christmas market in the Bull Ring and Cathedral precinct, Wakefield, West Yorkshire. It opened on 19 November 2009, but Wakefield council ordered it to leave by the 10 December. Only 30 of the 60 expected stalls arrived and residents had claimed it had no atmosphere and lacked German goods and entertainment.
